column1: iii. Natural Gas
Domestic natural gas production sustained its decline and reached 1.6 MTOE or 70.3
billion standard cubic feet of gas (BSCF) in 2024, which is 12.8 percent lower compared
to  the  previous  year.  This  decline  is  mainly  due  to  the  depletion  of  the  Malampaya
gas field, the country’s only indigenous source, which has seen reduced reserves and
lower production. Additionally, operational issues such as maintenance shutdowns and
infrastructure constraints have further reduced production levels.
Renewable Energy
i.  Geothermal
Geothermal energy continued to dominate the country’s renewable energy landscape
with a 13.4 percent share of TPES, albeit a moderate increase in levels  as it reached
9.3 MTOE  in  2024  compared  to  its  year-ago  level  of  9.2  MTOE.  As  of  end-2024,  33

geothermal  service  contracts  had  been  awarded,  reflecting  sustained 
interest 
in
the sector, as installed capacity remained at 1,951.7 MW15. It secured the Philippines’
position  as  the  world’s  third-largest  geothermal  producer  behind  the  United  States
and Indonesia.
ii. Biomass
The country’s total biomass16 supply grew steadily by 1.0 percent to 7.9 MTOE in 2024
and  equivalent  to  11.4  percent  share  in  the  energy  mix.  A  substantial  portion  (92.9
percent) of the biomass supply was directed toward end-use consumption, primarily

for  household  cooking, 
industrial  heating,  and  agricultural  processing,  while  the
remaining share was used for power generation. Around 63 biomass energy contracts
have been awarded that brought the cumulative biomass capacity to 595 MW as of
December 202417.
iii. Hydro
Hydropower output grew by 6.0 percent to 2.7 MTOE with a 3.9 percent contribution to
the energy mix during the year. This growth was mainly driven by the commissioning
of new small-scale hydro plants, improved rainfall that boosted water inflow to dams
and  rivers,  and  continued  government  support  through  the  Green  Energy  Auction
Program (GEAP). These developments also helped increase capacity of existing and
new hydropower facilities to 3,836 MW18 in 2024.
iv. Solar
Solar energy, despite a modest share of 0.5 percent in the energy mix, grew remarkably
by 49.8 percent during the year to 327.7 kTOE from 218.7 kTOE. This rapid expansion
was  fueled  by  accelerated  commissioning  of  new  solar  farms,  driven  by  investor-
friendly reforms and cost declines in solar technology. By year-end, installed capacity
reached 2,710 MW19, while 569 solar projects were approved for commercial or own-use
purposes that underscored the sustained momentum in the sector’s development.
